title: Fuel Cost Calculator: how it works, formula and examples
excerpt: Fuel Cost Calculator: Cost of fuel for any trip. Learn how to use it, the formula behind it, a worked example and answers to common questions.
content:
The [Fuel Cost Calculator](/fuel-cost-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Cost of fuel for any trip. Enter your trip distance, fuel economy and fuel price and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Estimate how much fuel a road trip will use and what it will cost, so you can budget or split costs fairly with passengers. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. Related Finance tools include [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator), [Mortgage Calculator](/mortgage-calculator) and [Car Loan Calculator](/car-loan-calculator). People also look for this tool as "gas cost calculator", "trip cost calculator", "petrol cost calculator".

## How to use the Fuel Cost Calculator

Start by entering your trip distance (km), then entering your fuel economy (L/100km) and finally entering your fuel price (per L). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. When you want a clean slate, Reset restores the defaults.

1. Enter your trip distance (km).
2. Enter your fuel economy (L/100km).
3. Enter your fuel price (per L).
4. Check the result — it updates instantly as you type.
5. Use Reset to start over with the default values.

## Formula

Fuel = distance × consumption ÷ 100. Cost = fuel × price.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Fuel Cost Calculator](/fuel-cost-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic. If the figures look wrong, check your inputs first — a misplaced decimal point is the usual culprit.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. 300 km at 7.5 L/100 km uses 22.5 L; at 1.60 per litre that's 36.00. Try the same figures in the [Fuel Cost Calculator](/fuel-cost-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. The steps are the same whatever numbers you use; only the figures change.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Trip distance: 300 km, Fuel economy: 7.5 L/100km, Fuel price: 1.60 per L), the [Fuel Cost Calculator](/fuel-cost-calculator) returns Trip fuel cost: 36, Fuel needed: 22.5 L, Cost per km: 0.12. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. Change any value and every figure updates instantly. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Loan Calculator](/loan-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Double the distance for a return trip.
- Highway driving is usually more efficient than city driving.

Keep these in mind and the figures will be as useful as the numbers you put in.

## Frequently asked questions

### How do I convert MPG to L/100km?

Divide 235.2 by US MPG. 30 MPG ≈ 7.84 L/100km. Try it with your own numbers in the [Fuel Cost Calculator](/fuel-cost-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Does speed affect fuel use?

Yes — consumption rises noticeably above about 90–100 km/h. Try it with your own numbers in the [Fuel Cost Calculator](/fuel-cost-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What formula does the Fuel Cost Calculator use?

Fuel = distance × consumption ÷ 100. Cost = fuel × price. You can see it in action in the [Fuel Cost Calculator](/fuel-cost-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What do I need to use the Fuel Cost Calculator?

Just Trip distance, Fuel economy and Fuel price. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
